name: building-ramp-visual
description: #555/#925: ordering a ramp queues progressive dig_ramp_segment excavation work instead of carving the whole corridor instantly, and each segment is now one horizontal Y-layer (bench) spanning the whole footprint, top to bottom, rather than one full-depth column at a time (#925) — a staffed, excavator-crewed rock_digger clears the topmost bench across the whole corridor before starting the next bench down. For this map/seed the origin:20,20 south length:6 depth:6 order carves surface Y=35 down to Y=30 (clearanceHeight 3 + max per-column depth 5), producing 8 layers. This scenario screenshots the corridor half-dug (orderedRampSegmentCount:4 — top 4 benches cleared across the full corridor, not one column dug to full depth) and again once every layer has landed (orderedRampSegmentCount:0), proving the dig happens bench-by-bench rather than column-by-column or in one synchronous burst.

steps.description: Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, the first of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants (balance.ts), before ordering any excavation work. #921: the Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls were removed from the DOM entirely -- runs as a bootstrap command instead.

Order the ramp — order-time validates and charges the whole corridor, then queues one dig_ramp_segment PendingAction per horizontal Y-layer (#925, reworking #555's one-per-column split) instead of carving anything yet. BuildMenu.ts's rampDepth field defaults to 8 (data-field="depth" on the ParamStrip, #925 visual-loop finding): two decrement clicks bring it to 6 before the drag+confirm, so the interaction-mode depth matches this step's own command:depth:6 fallback instead of silently reverting to the panel's default.

expect.note: 8 layers ordered (one per absolute Y row spanned by the corridor, topmost bench first — #925), none carved yet. Not 6 (the old one-per-column count): clearanceHeight (3) plus the deepest column's own target depth (5) span 8 distinct Y rows.

steps.description: Drain half the ordered layers — the crewed rock_digger clears one dig_ramp_segment bench at a time, topmost first (isRampSegmentClaimable still gates strictly by index, now a layer index rather than a column index). This step's own auto-captured screenshot is the mid-dig checkpoint: the corridor should show a flat bench across its full width and length at the current depth, not a single deep notch at one column while its neighbours sit untouched at the original surface. cameraFocus targets (20,23) — the corridor's midpoint (RAMP_WIDTH=3 centred on x:20, length 6 spanning z:20-26) — at a close distance so the excavated cross-section actually fills the frame instead of sitting as a small distant patch at the default orbiting camera (#925 visual-loop finding); it is re-issued here rather than relying on a prior step's framing because the shots loop below resets the camera (`__cameraReset`) after every step that has any shots.

expect.note: Mid-dig: the top 4 of the ramp's 8 layers have landed across the whole corridor footprint, the bottom 4 remain queued.

steps.description: Drain the remaining layers. This step's own auto-captured screenshot is the full-completion checkpoint: every layer carved, the ramp corridor complete end to end. cameraFocus re-issued (see the mid-dig step's note) so this checkpoint is framed the same as the mid-dig one, close enough to compare the finished smooth slope against the earlier bench.

expect.note: Ramp fully dug: every dig_ramp_segment action landed.
